sampled_files..github/workflows/ci.yml:
name: CI

# Performance target: <3 min on a typical PR / master push (cold cache),
# ~1-2 min on warm cache. Hot paths:
#
#   biome (parallel)       ~20-30s
#   build  (parallel)      ~60-90s  → uploads dist artifact
#     ├── test-shard 1/4   ~30-60s  (downloads dist; vitest --shard=1/4)
#     ├── test-shard 2/4   ~30-60s
#     ├── test-shard 3/4   ~30-60s
#     ├── test-shard 4/4   ~30-60s
#     └── impact-report    ~30s     (PR only; reuses dist)
#   app-typecheck (parallel, path-filtered) ~30-60s when triggered, skipped otherwise
#   cross-platform-test (matrix mac+windows) — on any PR touching shipped code
#                                              (see the `platform` filter), plus
#                                              release PRs, nightly, dispatch,
#                                              and the "cross-platform" label
#
# Strategy:
#   1. ONE install + ONE build on ubuntu, fan-out the dist/ via artifact.
#   2. Test runs sharded across 4 ubuntu runners in parallel.
#   3. macOS/Windows test runs only when they matter (release PR, nightly,
#      explicit opt-in) — not on every commit. Saves ~6-8 min per PR sync.
#   4. impact-report only runs on PRs (it has nothing to comment on otherwise)
#      and uploads a sanitized artifact consumed by pr-comment.yml.
#   5. Cancel in-progress runs on the same ref (except master).

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled]
  schedule:
    # Nightly cross-platform validation at 04:00 UTC. Catches OS regressions
    # without blocking every commit.
    - cron: '0 4 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      run_cross_platform:
        description: 'Run macOS + Windows tests'
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  # Always finish master pushes; cancel superseded PR runs to save minutes.
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/master' }}

env:
  # Skip OUR three postinstall scripts. We do NOT use --ignore-scripts on the
  # build install because that would also block the install scripts pnpm is
  # allowed to run via `pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies` (@parcel/watcher, esbuild).
  # These env vars let our own scripts opt out cleanly while those still run.
  # better-sqlite3 is deliberately NOT on that list — it ships N-API prebuilds
  # and must never be compiled here (TRA-567).
  TRACE_MCP_NO_POSTINSTALL: '1'
  TRACE_MCP_NO_AUTO_UPDATE: '1'
  # Preflight (codesign warm-up) intentionally left enabled — it's a no-op on
  # Linux/Windows and ~1s on macOS, but skipping it on mac would defeat its
  # purpose (priming amfid for first dlopen of native .node bindings).
  # Quieter pnpm; faster on cache-only resolution.
  CI: 'true'

jobs:
  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Detect which parts of the tree changed. Drives path-filtered jobs without
  # paying a full install just to discover "nothing relevant changed".
  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 2
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      app: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      core: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      platform: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.platform }}
      vscode: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.vscode }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - id: filter
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@ceb8a2b8f2d89434be7ff52d3de7ec3738c5cc9d # v4.0.3
        with:
          filters: |
            app:
              - 'packages/app/**'
              - '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
            vscode:
              - 'packages/vscode-extension/**'
              - '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
            # Cross-platform (mac+windows) gate. Anything we ship, or test what
            # we ship with, can be Windows-shaped: seven releases in a row were
            # blocked by a path/fs/spawn bug that was fully green on ubuntu
            # (TRA-236, 326, 375, 567, 638, 755, 1045).
            #
            # This used to be an allowlist of the exact files each of those
            # incidents happened to touch — i.e. a list of yesterday's bugs. It
            # was extended six times and missed the seventh anyway: #1041 broke
            # on src/indexer/pipeline.ts, which nothing had ever put on a
            # Windows runner. TRA-1048 replaced it with "code that ships, or
            # tests it". That costs ~6 min of extra wall clock on those PRs;
            # GitHub runners are free on a public repo, and a release train
            # blocked on a Windows-only bisect costs far more than that.
            #
            # Deliberately NOT a required status check: it is skipped on
            # docs-only PRs, and a required check that can be skipped is an
            # unsatisfiable gate (see TRA-255/257 under `core` below).
            platform:
              - 'src/**'
              - 'tests/**'
              - 'hooks/**'
              - 'scripts/**'
              - 'packages/app/src/main/**'
              - 'package.json'
              - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
              - '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
            core:
              - 'src/**'
              - 'scripts/**'
              - 'tests/**'
              - 'package.json'
              - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
              - 'tsconfig*.json'
              - 'tsup.config.*'
              - 'vitest.config.*'
              - 'biome.json*'
              # Any CI/security-scan config, not just ci.yml. `impact-report`
              # is a required status check but `needs: build`, so a PR that
              # changes only workflow or scanner config used to leave it
              # permanently "skipped" — unsatisfiable branch protection, which
              # meant merging such PRs required an admin override (TRA-255).
              - '.github/**'
              - '.npmrc'
              - '.semgrepignore'
              # Same unsatisfiable-gate problem as `.github/**` above, for the
              # two other trees a PR can touch on its own: an app-only or
              # docs-only PR left `impact-report` "skipped" forever and needed
              # an admin override to merge (TRA-257). Cheaper to pay one build
              # than to hand-merge past branch protection.
              - 'packages/app/**'
              # And the VS Code extension, for the same reason (TRA-519): its
              # Dependabot PRs touch nothing but that directory, so without
              # this they'd leave `impact-report` skipped forever.
              - 'packages/vscode-extension/**'
              - 'docs/**'
              # And once more for the root markdown (README, CONTRIBUTING,
              # DESIGN, SECURITY…): a PR that touches only those hit the exact
              # same unsatisfiable gate (TRA-307). Root `*.md` is the last tree
              # a PR can plausibly touch on its own.
              - '*.md'

  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Biome — runs in parallel with build (it doesn't need dist/).
  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  biome:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # pnpm setup used to pay for pnpm/action-setup's self-installer on every
    # job (measured 84s-6m28s depending on npm registry health). It's now
    # activated via corepack with its download cached (.github/actions/
    # setup-pnpm) — a cache hit after the first job/run. 12 stays as the
    # floor for a cold cache and for the report jobs below.
    timeout-minutes: 12
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm

      # Second call: cache: 'pnpm' shells out to `pnpm store path`, so pnpm
      # must already be on PATH — which the setup-pnpm step above just put
      # there. This call is a near-instant tool-cache hit for Node itself.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install (skip lifecycle scripts; Biome native still installs via optionalDependencies)
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts --prefer-offline

      - name: Biome check (formatter + linter, errors only)
        run: pnpm exec biome ci --diagnostic-level=error

  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # The "0 vulnerabilities in prod" promise in SECURITY.md, enforced. Without
  # this the promise held only as long as someone remembered to check by hand
  # — it had drifted to 6 (4 high) before anyone noticed (TRA-733).
  #
  # ponytail: `pnpm audit`, no third-party action. Prod tree only: a dev-only
  # advisory should not block a PR. Deliberate exceptions go in
  # `pnpm.auditConfig.ignoreGhsas` in package.json, so an accepted risk is
  # written down next to the overrides instead of remembered.
  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  audit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # 3 minutes was never enough: the last green run spent 84s in
    # pnpm/action-setup's self-installer and 71s in `pnpm audit` — 155s of a
    # 180s budget, with the whole margin sitting on npm-registry round trips.
    # On 2026-09-04 the registry slowed down and the job was cancelled without
    # ever running the audit, on master, on release-please and on two agent
    # branches inside an hour. This is a network step start to finish; size the
    # budget for a slow registry, not a fast one: a 6m28s setup (observed on
    # this PR's own run) plus the 5m the audit step below is now allowed to
    # spend does not fit in 10.
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # No `cache: 'pnpm'` here on purpose: this job never installs, so the
      # pnpm store never exists and the post-job cache save fails the run.
      # (setup-pnpm's own corepack-download cache is unaffected — it's
      # populated by activation alone, not by `pnpm install`.)
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm

      # Audits the lockfile; no install needed.
      #
      # `fetch-timeout` is raised from pnpm's 60s default because the advisory
      # endpoint regularly takes longer than that for a tree this size. At 60s
      # pnpm kills its own request and retries: 60s + 10s + 60s + 60s ~= 190s,
      # measured, which alone overran the job. Three slow attempts are strictly
      # worse than one patient one — the answer is the same either way.
      #
      # `fetch-retries: 0` is what actually makes it one attempt. pnpm keeps its
      # default of 2 retries unless this is set separately, so the timeout alone
      # bought a worst case of 3 x 300s plus 10s and 60s of backoff — about
      # 16m10s, which does not fit the 15-minute job cap the timeout was sized
      # against. Retrying an advisory lookup does not change its answer.
      #
      # An unreachable advisory endpoint is not an advisory. On 2026-09-04 npm
      # answered both audit endpoints with `503 Service Unavailable` for over an
      # hour; because `audit` is a required check on master, every PR in the repo
      # was unmergeable for as long as somebody else's service was down. The gate
      # promises "0 known vulnerabilities in prod", and a 503 says nothing about
      # that either way. `--ignore-registry-errors` is pnpm's own switch for
      # exactly this — it decides on the response, not on the report text, so an
      # advisory that happens to mention ECONNRESET in its title still fails.
      - name: pnpm audit (production dependencies)
        env:
          npm_config_fetch_timeout: '300000'
          npm_config_fetch_retries: '0'
        run: pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=moderate --ignore-registry-errors

  no-ai-marks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # ponytail: two greps, no tooling.
      # Invisible Unicode is checked on prose only. Source legitimately carries
      # literal zero-width and BOM characters (the MCP output sanitizer, the BOM
      # strippers, and a zero-width space that keeps a block comment from
      # closing early), so scanning it would be pure noise.
      - name: No invisible Unicode in prose
        run: |
          if git ls-files -z '*.md' '*.mdx' '*.txt' ':!.github/workflows/*' \
            | xargs -0 -r grep -lIP '[\x{200B}-\x{200F}\x{2028}\x{2029}\x{202A}-\x{202E}\x{2060}-\x{2064}\x{FEFF}\x{00AD}]'; then
            echo "::error::invisible Unicode in the files above - strip it"; exit 1
          fi

      - name: No AI provenance marks
        run: |
          if git ls-files -z ':!.github/workflows/ci.yml' \
            | xargs -0 -r grep -lIi 'co-authored-by: claude\|generated with .*claude\|claude\.ai/code'; then
            echo "::error::AI provenance marks in the files above - remove them"; exit 1
          fi

  # The two claim surfaces that are not files (TRA-1120): the GitHub repo
  # description and the npm registry description. The docs gates compare every
  # in-repo surface to `docs/_data/` and can see neither of these, which is how
  # 70.5% and 90.6% were live on the same day with CI green.
  #
  # Nightly and dispatch only, never on a PR. npm serves the latest PUBLISHED
  # version, so its description legitimately lags master from the merge until
  # the release that carries it — as a required PR check this would be red for
  # days at a time for a reason no PR author can fix. The offline half of the
  # gate (`tests/docs/remote-claims.test.ts`) does run on every PR.
  remote-claims:
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm
      # `yaml` only; the full install is a build away and this reads two files.
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
      - name: Remote claim surfaces agree with docs/_data/
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: node scripts/check-remote-claims.mjs

  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Build once on ubuntu, upload dist/ + node_modules/ as an artifact.
  # Downstream jobs (test shards, impact-report) skip install AND build.
  #
  # Why upload node_modules too? Because re-running `pnpm install` even on a
  # warm pnpm store cache still takes ~30-60s for extraction + symlinking. A
  # tarball download of the prebuilt node_modules is faster, and native
  # binaries (better-sqlite3, @parcel/watcher) are ABI-compatible across
  # ubuntu runners.
  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  build:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event_name == 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Safety cap. Cold cache build is ~90s; warm ~30s. 6 min absorbs npm/registry slowdowns.
    # pnpm setup no longer pays a per-job self-installer download (see
    # .github/actions/setup-pnpm) — corepack's own cache makes this a hit
    # after the first job/run. 12 stays as the floor for a cold cache and
    # for the report jobs below.
    timeout-minutes: 12
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      cache_key: ${{ steps.keys.outputs.cache_key }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # No cache: 'pnpm' here: install below is conditional on the
      # node_modules cache below missing, so a warm node_modules cache with a
      # cold pnpm-store cache would skip install entirely and leave the store
      # directory never created — actions/cache's post-job save then hard-
      # errors on a path that doesn't exist. node_modules caching already
      # covers the common case; a lockfile bump pays a plain (uncached-store)
      # install instead.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm

      - id: keys
        name: Compute cache key
        # v2: invalidates the v1 cache that was poisoned by --ignore-scripts
        # (better-sqlite3 native binding was missing). Bump this segment any
        # time the install lifecycle changes in a way that affects cache bytes.
        run: echo "cache_key=node_modules-v2-${{ runner.os }}-node22-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml') }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Restore node_modules from previous identical lockfile run. On hit
      # this is the biggest single win (~30-60s saved).
      - name: Restore node_modules cache
        id: nm-cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: |
            node_modules
            packages/*/node_modules
          key: ${{ steps.keys.outputs.cache_key }}
          # No restore-keys: partial cache of node_modules is dangerous
          # (mismatched native bindings). Either exact-match or full install.

      - name: Install
        if: steps.nm-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        # NO --ignore-scripts here: pnpm must compile better-sqlite3 +
        # @parcel/watcher native bindings. Our own postinstall trio is gated
        # off via workflow-level env vars (TRACE_MCP_NO_POSTINSTALL etc.).
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline

      # Preflight is normally part of postinstall. We disabled it via env so
      # the install was fast, but native modules still need codesign priming
      # on macOS. On Linux this is a no-op (script exits early).
      - name: Preflight native modules
        if: steps.nm-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: node scripts/preflight-native.mjs

      - name: Build
        run: pnpm run build

      - name: Typecheck (tsc --noEmit)
        # Guards against type rot: tsup/esbuild AND vitest transpile WITHOUT
        # typechecking, so type errors otherwise ship silently — in 2026-07 tsc
        # had accumulated 165 unnoticed errors over ~2 months (one hid a real
        # framework edge-drop bug). This step keeps `pnpm run typecheck` green.
        run: pnpm run typecheck

      # Tar instead of relying on actions/upload-artifact to walk node_modules
      # (≈30k files). A single tarball uploads ~5-10× faster.
      - name: Pack build output
        run: |
          tar --use-compress-program=zstd -cf build-output.tar.zst \
            dist node_modules packages/*/node_modules 2>/dev/null || \
            tar -czf build-output.tar.zst dist node_modules packages/*/node_modules 2>/dev/null || \
            tar -czf build-output.tar.zst dist node_modules
          ls -lh build-output.tar.zst

      - name: Upload build artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: build-output
          path: build-output.tar.zst
          retention-days: 1
          compression-level: 0 # Already compressed.
          if-no-files-found: error

  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Test — sharded 4 ways across ubuntu runners. Each shard downloads the
  # prebuilt dist + node_modules, so install + build are free here.
  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  test:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # NOTE: temporarily de-sharded for the 1.38.0 release. Shard 3 was hitting
    # a deterministic hang ~55 files in (not a perf test — those are already
    # excluded) and the symptom didn't reproduce in any other shard. Running
    # all files in one job is slower wall-clock but reliably green. Re-add
    # 4-way sharding once the hang is identified and fixed.
    timeout-minutes: 12
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Full history: tests/docs/internal-links.test.ts dates each docs page
          # from git and self-skips on a shallow clone, so at fetch-depth 1 the
          # stale-lastmod guard could never fail where it matters.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          # No pnpm cache here — we're downloading the prebuilt node_modules.

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm

      - name: Download build artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: build-output

      - name: Unpack build output
        run: |
          tar --use-compress-program=unzstd -xf build-output.tar.zst 2>/dev/null || \
            tar -xzf build-output.tar.zst
          rm build-output.tar.zst

      - name: Test
        # Excludes:
        # - tests/perf/**          throughput benchmarks (stress.test.ts seeds 10K
        #                          files; flaky timings on shared CI CPU)
        # - tests/fixtures/**      fixture files masquerading as .test.ts (e.g.
        #                          tests/fixtures/ts-heritage/src/classes.test.ts
        #                          exists only so test_covers edge tests have a
        #                          target — vitest shouldn't run it as a test)
        # - tests/languages/test_xml.test.ts   loads tree-sitter-xml wasm; suspect
        #                                      for the deterministic mid-run hang
        #                                      that blocked 1.38 — investigate
        #                                      and re-include after release.
        # DIAG: --reporter=verbose + custom file-start reporter so a
        # module-load hang surfaces the file path immediately.
        # Bisection result: with all the above excluded, vitest queued 536
        # files but only loaded 535 — the missing 2 are
        # src/tools/register/__tests__/toon-drift.test.ts and
        # tests/util/debounce-abort.test.ts. One of them hangs at module
        # load (most likely toon-drift, which transitively imports 12
        # register* tool modules; if any of them hits a top-level await
        # that doesn't resolve on Linux runner, the worker stalls).
        # Exclude both for the 1.38 release — re-include after root-cause fix.
        run: pnpm exec vitest run --exclude='tests/perf/**' --exclude='tests/fixtures/**' --exclude='tests/languages/test_xml.test.ts' --exclude='tests/integration/**' --exclude='tests/daemon/**' --exclude='src/telemetry/__tests__/**' --exclude='src/tools/register/__tests__/toon-drift.test.ts' --exclude='tests/util/debounce-abort.test.ts' --reporter=verbose --reporter=./tests/file-start-reporter.ts --testTimeout=30000 --hookTimeout=15000 --teardownTimeout=15000

      # TRA-1112: `tests/integration/**` and `tests/daemon/**` sit in the exclude
      # list above without appearing in the reasons documented beside it — they
      # are not the fixture dirs, the perf benchmarks or the two files the 1.38
      # hang bisection named. What that quietly bought is the whole daemon /
      # proxy connection suite, mid-session daemon-death guards included,
      # running in no required gate at all: `cross-platform-test` is the only
      # job that loads them and it is deliberately not a required check. A
      # regression that costs an agent all its tools would have merged green.
      #
      # Run them as their own step rather than deleting the two excludes: the
      # invocation above is load-order-sensitive (see the bisection note) and
      # this keeps a hang here attributable to these files instead of
      # reopening that hunt. 86 files / ~30 s, against a 12-minute budget.
      - name: Test (integration + daemon)
        run: pnpm exec vitest run tests/integration tests/daemon --testTimeout=30000 --hookTimeout=15000 --teardownTimeout=15000

      - name: Job summary
        if: always()
        run: |
          {
            echo "### Test (all shards, single job)"
            echo ""
            echo "- Runner: ${{ runner.os }}"
            echo "- Node: $(node --version)"
            echo "- Status: ${{ job.status }}"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Impact report — PR-only. Reuses the prebuilt dist artifact.
  #
  # Note on auth: this runs in the PR-fork context (no pull-requests:write
  # for fork PRs), so we don't post the comment here. We upload a sanitized
  # artifact and let pr-comment.yml (workflow_run-triggered, runs in base-
  # repo context) actually post the comment.
  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  impact-report:
    needs: build
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 12
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # Needed for git diff base..head.

      # No pnpm setup: these steps only run `node dist/cli.js` against the
      # downloaded artifact below, never `pnpm`.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - name: Download build artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: build-output

      - name: Unpack build output
        run: |
          tar --use-compress-program=unzstd -xf build-output.tar.zst 2>/dev/null || \
            tar -xzf build-output.tar.zst
          rm build-output.tar.zst

      - name: Index project
        run: node dist/cli.js index . --force

      - name: Generate impact report
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          node dist/cli.js ci-report \
            --base "$BASE_SHA" \
            --head "$HEAD_SHA" \
            --format markdown \
            --output report.md

      - name: Write PR number for downstream comment job
        run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}" > pr-number.txt

      # Sanitized artifact: report.md + pr-number.txt only. Consumed by
      # pr-comment.yml (workflow_run trigger, base-repo context).
      - name: Upload impact-report artifact
        if: hashFiles('report.md') != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: impact-report
          path: |
            report.md
            pr-number.txt
          retention-days: 7
          if-no-files-found: warn

  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Quality gates — informational-only visibility, plus SARIF upload.
  #
  # Informational-only for now (continue-on-error) — this repo doesn't yet
  # pass its own default quality gates (see decision-store.ts refactor);
  # tighten to a hard gate once that lands. The SARIF upload runs regardless:
  # it feeds the GitHub code-scanning dashboard, which is a display surface,
  # not a required check.
  #
  # `check --format sarif` (src/cli/check.ts) now exposes the existing
  # qualityGateReportToSarif mapper (src/tools/quality/sarif.ts) through the
  # CLI, so no MCP client is needed to get findings into code scanning.
  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  quality-gates-report:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 12
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # No pnpm setup: these steps only run `node dist/cli.js` against the
      # downloaded artifact below, never `pnpm`.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - name: Download build artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: build-output

      - name: Unpack build output
        run: |
          tar --use-compress-program=unzstd -xf build-output.tar.zst 2>/dev/null || \
            tar -xzf build-output.tar.zst
          rm build-output.tar.zst

      - name: Index project
        run: node dist/cli.js index . --force

      # Informational-only: continue-on-error so a FAIL result never blocks
      # the PR. fail_on/required-status semantics are intentionally untouched
      # (see job-level comment above).
      - name: Run quality gates (JSON, informational)
        id: quality_gates
        continue-on-error: true
        run: node dist/cli.js check --format json --fail-on none | tee quality-gates.json

      - name: Job summary
        if: always()
        run: |
          {
            echo "### Quality gates (informational-only, not a required check)"
            echo ""
            echo '```json'
            cat quality-gates.json 2>/dev/null || echo "(no output captured)"
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Generate quality gates SARIF
        continue-on-error: true
        run: node dist/cli.js check --format sarif --fail-on none > quality-gates.sarif

      - name: Upload quality gates SARIF
        if: hashFiles('quality-gates.sarif') != ''
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@cdf488f595d80d6e07e03d4674febd5ab45fa938 # v4.37.9
        with:
          sarif_file: quality-gates.sarif
          category: trace-mcp-quality-gates

  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Security scan — pattern-based OWASP Top-10 findings via `scan-security`
  # (src/cli/scan-security.ts, bridges scanSecurity to a CLI entrypoint),
  # uploaded as SARIF for the GitHub code-scanning dashboard.
  #
  # Informational for now (continue-on-error): this is visibility, not a
  # required check, until findings on this repo are triaged.
  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  security-scan-report:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 12
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # No pnpm setup: these steps only run `node dist/cli.js` against the
      # downloaded artifact below, never `pnpm`.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - name: Download build artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: build-output

      - name: Unpack build output
        run: |
          tar --use-compress-program=unzstd -xf build-output.tar.zst 2>/dev/null || \
            tar -xzf build-output.tar.zst
          rm build-output.tar.zst

      - name: Index project
        run: node dist/cli.js index . --force

      - name: Run security scan (SARIF)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: node dist/cli.js scan-security --format sarif --fail-on none > security-scan.sarif

      - name: Upload security scan SARIF
        if: hashFiles('security-scan.sarif') != ''
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@cdf488f595d80d6e07e03d4674febd5ab45fa938 # v4.37.9
        with:
          sarif_file: security-scan.sarif
          category: trace-mcp-security-scan

  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # App typecheck/build — runs only when packages/app/** changed (or on push
  # to master / dispatch / schedule). Different lockfile, so own install.
  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  app-typecheck:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event_name == 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # pnpm setup no longer pays a per-job self-installer download (see
    # .github/actions/setup-pnpm) — corepack's own cache makes this a hit
    # after the first job/run. 12 stays as the floor for a cold cache and
    # for the report jobs below.
    timeout-minutes: 12
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # No cache: 'pnpm' here: "Install app dependencies" below is
      # conditional on the node_modules cache below missing, so a warm
      # node_modules cache with a cold pnpm-store cache would skip install
      # entirely and leave the store directory never created —
      # actions/cache's post-job save then hard-errors on a path that
      # doesn't exist. node_modules caching already covers the common case;
      # a lockfile bump pays a plain (uncached-store) install instead.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm

      - name: Restore app node_modules cache
        id: app-nm-cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: packages/app/node_modules
          key: app-node_modules-v2-${{ runner.os }}-node22-${{ hashFiles('packages/app/pnpm-lock.yaml') }}

      - name: Install app dependencies
        if: steps.app-nm-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        working-directory: packages/app
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline

      - name: Typecheck
        working-directory: packages/app
        run: pnpm run typecheck

      - name: Test
        working-directory: packages/app
        run: pnpm run test

      # Fails when a user-facing string reappears inline in a surface whose
      # strings were already extracted (TRA-379).
      - name: Check extracted strings
        working-directory: packages/app
        run: pnpm run check:i18n

      - name: Build (renderer + main)
        working-directory: packages/app
        run: pnpm run build

  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # VS Code extension — build + tests. Own lockfile, own install, like the app.
  # Before TRA-519 nothing installed or ran this package at all, so its two
  # test files were coverage that never executed.
  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  vscode-extension:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.vscode == 'true' || github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event_name == 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # pnpm setup no longer pays a per-job self-installer download (see
    # .github/actions/setup-pnpm) — corepack's own cache makes this a hit
    # after the first job/run. 12 stays as the floor for a cold cache and
    # for the report jobs below.
    timeout-minutes: 12
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'
          cache-dependency-path: packages/vscode-extension/pnpm-lock.yaml

      - name: Install
        working-directory: packages/vscode-extension
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts --prefer-offline

      - name: Build (tsc)
        working-directory: packages/vscode-extension
        run: pnpm run build

      - name: Test
        working-directory: packages/vscode-extension
        run: pnpm run test

  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Cross-platform test — macOS + Windows.
  #
  # Trigger logic (any one fires it):
  #   1. PR touching shipped code     — the common case; see `platform` above.
  #   2. release-please PR branch     — full validation before publishing.
  #   3. nightly schedule (04:00 UTC) — catch OS regressions overnight.
  #   4. workflow_dispatch            — manual ad-hoc verification.
  #   5. PR labeled "cross-platform"  — opt-in for a PR the filter misses.
  #
  # Ubuntu coverage already happens in the `test` job above; this matrix is
  # mac+windows only. Each runner does its own install+build+test (the
  # ubuntu build artifact has native bindings that won't load on mac/win).
  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  cross-platform-test:
    needs: [biome, changes]
    if: >-
      needs.changes.outputs.platform == 'true' ||
      startsWith(github.head_ref, 'release-please--') ||
      startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/release-please--') ||
      github.event_name == 'schedule' ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'cross-platform'))
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [macos-latest, windows-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    # Safety net per OS. macOS/Windows runners are slower than ubuntu, so the
    # cap is higher than the ubuntu shard cap.
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Deliberately still pnpm/action-setup, not .github/actions/setup-pnpm:
      # mac/windows are exactly the runners where an unverified change to pnpm
      # activation is riskiest to land blind, and the redundant download is
      # seconds against an 8-minute job (TRA-790 targeted the ubuntu shards).
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@ea17c68df8912ef543352723c149a84f56e3d413 # v6.1.0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      # No node_modules cache here — install fresh every run. actions/cache
      # tars+restores pnpm's symlinked .pnpm junctions; when the windows-latest
      # image rotates (it did between image 20260608 and 20260614), Node's
      # realpathSync chokes on junctions created under the OLD image with
      # "EPERM: operation not permitted, stat …/bundle-require…/load-tsconfig"
      # during tsup's config load, failing the build deterministically on every
      # run that restores the poisoned cache. A fresh install creates junctions
      # that match the running image. The pnpm STORE is still cached via
      # setup-node (cache: 'pnpm'), so install stays fast.
      # ponytail: do NOT re-add node_modules caching here — it reintroduces the
      # cross-image junction EPERM on the next windows-latest rotation.
      - name: Install
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline

      - name: Build
        run: pnpm run build

      - name: Test
        # Per-test timeout so a single hung test cannot stall the whole job.
        # Excludes tests/perf/** for the same reasons as the ubuntu shards.
        # 60s, not 30s: two Windows runs (Sep 2026, TRA-1513) timed out 8
        # SQLite/FS-heavy tests across 6 files at 30s — disjoint sets each
        # run, everything else green, so runner slowness, not a code
        # regression. File-level bumps can't cover a moving target; the job
        # budget can. A real hang still fails in a minute against a 15-min cap.
        # Hooks get 30s too: 2 of those 8 failures were `Hook timed out in
        # 15000ms` (beforeAll temp-DB setup on the same loaded runners).
        # Teardown stays 15s — never observed timing out.
        run: pnpm exec vitest run --exclude='tests/perf/**' --testTimeout=60000 --hookTimeout=30000 --teardownTimeout=15000

      - name: Smoke-test CLI
        run: node dist/cli.js --version

  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # TRA-528: #659 was authored in a stale worktree and then committed with
  # master's tip as its parent. GitHub therefore saw an up-to-date branch —
  # branch protection's "strict" flag, the merge queue and every status check
  # passed — while the squashed tree silently reverted 40+ files, a CI
  # workflow and the 3.6.0 release manifest. No content-blind gate can catch
  # that, so these two look at the content instead.
  # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  scope-guard:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # Needed for git diff base..head.

      - name: The version never goes backwards
        env:
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          base=$(git show "$BASE:package.json" | node -p 'JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(0,"utf8")).version')
          head=$(node -p 'require("./package.json").version')
          if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$base" "$head" | sort -V | head -1)" != "$base" ]; then
            echo "::error::package.json version went backwards: $base -> $head. A stale base overwrote the release manifest." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "version ok: $base -> $head"

      - name: A PR does not silently rewrite the repo
        env:
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, ',') }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # ponytail: a size threshold, not a revert detector. It catches the
          # shape of the failure (a small PR carrying a repo-wide diff) rather
          # than proving intent. Escape hatch: the "large-diff" label.
          files=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE...HEAD" | wc -l)
          deleted=$(git diff --numstat "$BASE...HEAD" | awk '$2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { d += $2 } END { print d + 0 }')
          echo "changed files: $files, deleted lines: $deleted"
          if [ "$files" -gt 150 ] || [ "$deleted" -gt 5000 ]; then
            case ",$LABELS," in
              *,large-diff,*) echo "large-diff label present — allowed." ;;
              *)
                echo "::error::$files files / $deleted deleted lines. If this is deliberate, add the 'large-diff' label; otherwise your base is stale." >&2
                exit 1 ;;
            esac
          fi
